purpose: Gate implementation on intent-appropriate media, art-directed dominant assets, truthful provenance, and typography with explicit brand and functional roles.
requiredEvidence: asset manifest with routing decisions and provenance
materialization record with local paths, SHA-256 hashes, and rendered use for every required asset
SVG absence audit covering project filenames, source text, rendered DOM, library renderers, and network requests
type manifest with role assignments and real font metadata
reference typography contract with family class, width, contrast, measures, authored line structure, and script pairing when a reference is adopted
document.fonts.ready, document.fonts.check, computed role styles, loading, fallback, accessibility, and transfer-budget evidence

anchors.0: Dominant assets or typography are missing, deceptive, inaccessible, or use a blocked medium.
anchors.1: Assets and type load, but routing, provenance, quality, or role discipline is materially weak.
anchors.2: The system is usable with noticeable medium, integration, typography, or responsive gaps.
anchors.3: Media and typography fit their roles with minor non-blocking limitations.
anchors.4: Every dominant visual and type role is intentional, traceable, responsive, accessible, performant, and visibly integrated.

checks.question: Was each dominant visual routed to a medium appropriate to its content and behavior?
checks.passCondition: New images and artwork are materialized as local PNG, JPEG, WebP, or AVIF raster assets through the available image generator; semantic HTML, CSS, and Canvas are reserved for simple UI or runtime geometry; other runtimes are used only for roles they support and are configured without SVG renderers or fallbacks.
failureSignals: image or artwork exists only as prompt text, placeholder, CSS proxy, Canvas proxy, or vector substitute instead of a real generated raster
heavy spatial renderer used for a simple static shape
chart or interactive visualization lacks an accessible HTML data view
medium choice lacks an intent explanation

checks.question: Is the entire implemented site free of SVG files, markup, payloads, renderers, and fallbacks?
checks.passCondition: The project contains no .svg files or references, inline <svg> nodes, image/svg+xml MIME or data URI payloads, SVG CSS masks/backgrounds/clip paths, icon-library SVG output, animation or chart SVG renderers, SVG fallbacks, rendered SVG DOM nodes, or SVG network requests at any required viewport.
failureSignals: any .svg file or .svg path appears in implemented source or public assets
inline <svg> markup or an SVG DOM node is present
data:image/svg+xml or image/svg+xml appears in source, computed styles, responses, or requests
icon, chart, animation, or visualization library inserts or exports SVG
an SVG placeholder, poster, mask, clip path, background, fallback, or data URI is used
evidence: desktop, tablet, and mobile rendered DOM inspection
browser network request and MIME evidence
computed styles and runtime renderer configuration

checks.question: Are dominant assets traceable and ready for production use?
checks.passCondition: Each asset records source or generation provenance, local path or stable source, rights status, dimensions, format, readiness score, responsive variants, accessible fallback, and transfer-budget impact.
failureSignals: unknown provenance or rights
missing source or generated-file relationship
unexplained readiness score
missing fallback or responsive behavior
dominant asset exceeds the declared transfer budget without justification

checks.question: Is every required production asset a real, independently verified local file?
checks.passCondition: Every required food, product, character, hero-object, editorial, and other raster role is materialized through the available image generator as a separate local PNG, JPEG, WebP, or AVIF production file with valid format, dimensions, provenance, SHA-256, responsive behavior, and rendered-use evidence.
failureSignals: asset status remains planned or prompt-only
missing or empty expected output
direction-frame image or crop reused as a production asset
placeholder, SVG proxy, CSS proxy, gradient, or remote chat image used for a required raster role
local file lacks a matching SHA-256 or rendered-use record

checks.question: Do crop, edge treatment, scale, lighting, and placement make dominant assets part of the composition?
checks.passCondition: Assets align with the focal relationship, retain quality at required viewports, and act as anchors, bridges, interrupts, reveals, or utilities rather than placed decoration.
failureSignals: stock-looking or low-resolution dominant image
cutout edge halos or mismatched lighting
object floats beside content without structural role
mobile crop removes the visual thesis

checks.question: Does every typeface have an explicit brand or functional role?
checks.passCondition: Display, text, data, and interface roles are intentionally assigned; when reference evidence exists, family class, stroke contrast, width, x-height, role ownership, case, tracking, measures, authored line counts, numerals, and script companions are extracted and hard-gated instead of reduced to mood tags.
failureSignals: unexplained system-default typography in quality mode
typeface selected only because its name matches the desired style
monospace used for all roles
too many unrelated families
reference uses serif-led editorial roles but the selected system collapses to a neutral sans
a high aggregate router score is used to excuse family-class, width, contrast, role, or line-count drift

checks.question: Do the declared font files and authored styles match what the browser can render?
checks.passCondition: Project-local WOFF2 files load, document.fonts.ready resolves, document.fonts.check passes for every declared family, computed role families match the manifest, real weights and styles are declared, font-synthesis is none, script coverage fits the content, and metric-compatible fallbacks are planned.
failureSignals: missing or failed font request
declared weight or italic file does not exist
content script is unsupported
layout shift or unreadable fallback
synthetic bold or italic changes the intended hierarchy
document.fonts.check fails or the computed family reveals browser fallback
multilingual copy falls into a generic family that contradicts the reference

checks.question: Does the implemented type system preserve the adopted reference relationships?
checks.passCondition: Family class, stroke contrast, width, x-height, role ownership, case, tracking, headline and body measures, authored line counts, accent-word treatment, numerals, script pairing, and responsive transformation match the reference-conditioned type contract at every required viewport.
failureSignals: headline line count or inline accent treatment drifts from the adopted reference
body, display, place-name, or numeral roles use the wrong family class
display size is used to disguise the wrong width or stroke contrast
critical copy wraps accidentally rather than following authored breaks and measures
a multilingual role falls into an incompatible generic browser fallback
evidence: computed role typography and line counts

checks.question: Does typography visibly support hierarchy, brand voice, reading, and responsive composition?
checks.passCondition: Personality, scale, spacing, line length, wrapping, contrast, and object–type integration remain deliberate and readable across all required viewports.
failureSignals: display face weakens product tone
orphaned or collision-prone headline
body line length harms reading
type and imagery compete without hierarchy
mobile typography is only a uniformly scaled desktop system

blockingRules: Any SVG file, reference, markup node, MIME/data payload, CSS use, icon-library output, runtime renderer, fallback, rendered DOM node, or network request blocks implementation and acceptance.
New images and artwork must be real image-generator-produced PNG, JPEG, WebP, or AVIF files; HTML, CSS, and Canvas are limited to simple UI or runtime geometry.
Every required dominant production asset must be materialized as a separate local hash-bound file; planned, placeholder, or direction-frame-derived assets block implementation and acceptance.
Router scores are readiness evidence, not a substitute for rendered visual judgment.
A reference-conditioned family-class, width, contrast, role, fallback, or line-count mismatch blocks acceptance regardless of the aggregate typography score.
Unknown provenance, missing font files, inaccessible fallbacks, or unsupported script coverage block acceptance.
